title: wirekit core - error, retry, rate limit, pooled client, tracing, auth

overview.problemStatement: The workspace holds one crate, dado. Every provider integration named in catalogue/ will be a wirekit module, but wirekit does not exist: there is no shared error type, retry policy, rate limiter, HTTP client pool, tracing story, or auth layer. Without that shared core, each first-publish provider (NOAA, Twilio, SendGrid, Slack) would grow its own error enum, retry loop, and auth handling, which is the fragmentation wirekit exists to remove and a direct violation of CON-207.
overview.proposedSolution: Add a new workspace crate, crates/wirekit at version 0.1.0, that ships only the provider-independent core: a #[non_exhaustive] WirekitError with stable W#### codes; one retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter, 3 attempts by default, retry on 5xx/429/network, honor Retry-After, never retry other 4xx); a hand-rolled per-provider token bucket; one shared reqwest::Client with HTTPS-only base URLs and an injection path; an auth layer with Bearer, Basic, API key (header and query), HMAC, and OAuth2 client credentials over a redacting Secret wrapper; tracing events for request start, finish, retry, rate-limit hit, and error; and one request pipeline (auth -> rate limit -> retry -> send -> decode) including the body-level error hook. Provider modules, examples, docs, and publishing belong to BP-006 to BP-010.
overview.targetAudience: External Rust developers installing wirekit 0.1.0 who expect one error type, one retry policy, and one auth layer across providers, plus the provider modules (BP-006 to BP-009) and the M2/M3 crates that consume this contract.
assumptions: The crate name wirekit is available on crates.io; it MUST be re-checked immediately before publication (CON-111). Availability is not verified by this feature.
The chosen dependency versions are MSRV 1.85 compatible and stay so; an MSRV CI job guards this (CON-102).
rustls is the preferred TLS backend; native-tls is a documented alternative, not the default.
Provider integrations remain feature-gated modules of wirekit, never separate crates (CON-104).
The core is always compiled; default = [] means no provider module enabled, not no core.
The dado dependency in the backlog is a sequencing dependency, not a code dependency; wirekit does not call dado.
Test authoring belongs to /sdrive:test, not this feature's implementation tasks.
Actual publication happens in BP-010 from main after review and archive.
outOfScope: Provider modules and their feature flags (twilio, sendgrid, noaa, slack, and every other catalogue/ provider)
OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE and browser redirects (BP-015 owns the PKCE helper per CON-212)
Examples, a provider matrix, a docs site, and the changelog (BP-010)
Cross-process quota state (quota-ledger), webhook verification and delivery state (hookgate), and the tenant/provider registry (platform-core)
Streaming uploads/downloads, WebSocket transports, and multipart file transfer beyond a single-body request
Application domain types, billing rules, and product workflows (CON-106)

userStories.title: Handle every provider failure with one error type
userStories.want: one WirekitError type that every provider maps into
userStories.benefit: I write one error handler instead of one per provider

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a provider response with a non-2xx status, when the pipeline maps the failure, then it returns WirekitError::Api { status, code, message } and no provider-specific error type appears in the public API.
Given any WirekitError, when code() is called, then it returns a stable &'static str of the form W####, and Display renders the code with a message.
Given any WirekitError, when Debug and Display are printed, then no credential, token, or raw request/response body appears.
Given the WirekitError enum, when a consumer matches it with a wildcard arm, then the match compiles, proving #[non_exhaustive].
Given WirekitError, when used with ? or as Box<dyn std::error::Error>, then it implements std::error::Error and exposes source() for wrapped causes.

userStories.title: Get the same retry behavior from every provider
userStories.want: one retry policy that applies everywhere
userStories.benefit: I am not debugging why one provider retries and another does not

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a 5xx response and the default policy, when the request is executed, then it is retried up to 3 attempts total, and the final failure is WirekitError::Api carrying the last status.
Given a 429 response with a Retry-After header, when the request is retried, then the delay is at least the header value, and an exhausted policy yields WirekitError::RateLimit { retry_after }.
Given a 400, 401, 403, or 404 response, when executed, then no retry occurs and the error returns immediately.
Given a network or timeout failure, when executed, then it is retried and ends as WirekitError::Network or WirekitError::Timeout.
Given the retry policy, when delays are computed, then they grow exponentially with bounded jitter and stay within the configured bounds.
Given a retry, when it occurs, then a tracing event records the attempt number and the delay.

userStories.title: Respect per-provider rate limits
userStories.want: rate limiting handled in one place
userStories.benefit: I do not build rate limiting per API

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a configured per-provider token bucket, when requests exceed the configured rate, then the limiter throttles them so the rate is not exceeded.
Given two providers with different rate configurations, when both send requests, then each uses its own bucket and its own override.
Given a rate-limit hit, when it occurs, then a tracing metric event is emitted.
Given an empty bucket, when a request waits for a token, then the async task yields instead of blocking the runtime thread (no std::thread::sleep).

userStories.title: Share one HTTP client pool
userStories.benefit: connections are reused and memory is bounded

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given no injected client, when two providers send requests, then they share one reqwest::Client and therefore one connection pool.
Given a caller-injected reqwest::Client, when a request is sent, then the injected client is used verbatim and no second pool is created.
Given the client builder, when timeouts, TLS, a proxy, and default headers are configured, then those settings apply to requests.
Given an http:// base URL, when a request is prepared, then it is rejected with WirekitError::InvalidConfig before any socket is opened.
Given the default configuration, when the client is built, then a request timeout and connection-pool limits are applied.

userStories.title: Apply authentication consistently
userStories.benefit: every provider using the same scheme reuses it

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a bearer token, when a request is sent, then Authorization: Bearer <token> is applied.
Given basic credentials, when a request is sent, then Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)> is applied.
Given an API key configured for a header, when a request is sent, then the configured header carries the key.
Given an API key configured for the query string, when a request is sent, then the key is added as a query parameter.
Given the HMAC scheme, when a request is signed, then the signature is computed over the canonical raw request bytes and compared with a constant-time routine.
Given OAuth2 client credentials, when a request is made without a valid token, then a token is fetched, cached, and reused, and is refreshed before expiry.
Given an auth or secret type, when Debug/Display are printed, then the secret renders as ***, and no secret field implements Serialize.

userStories.title: Observe every call
userStories.benefit: I can plug in OpenTelemetry, Datadog, or Jaeger once

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a request, when it starts, then a tracing event with the method and the redacted URL is emitted.
Given a completed request, when it finishes, then a tracing event records the duration.
Given a retry, a rate-limit hit, or an error, when it occurs, then the matching tracing event is emitted.
Given any of these events, when they are recorded, then no credential or token appears in the output.

userStories.title: Implement a provider against one pipeline
userStories.want: to declare a URL, method, body, and response type
userStories.benefit: I do not reimplement auth, retry, rate limiting, tracing, or error mapping

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a provider that declares a URL, method, body, and response type, when it executes, then the pipeline applies auth, rate limit, retry, send, and decode in that order.
Given a successful response, when decoded, then the caller's typed value is returned via serde.
Given HTTP 200 with a body-level error (Slack ok: false or a GraphQL errors[] array), when the body hook is configured, then WirekitError::Api is returned instead of a success (CON-213).
Given a malformed body, when decoding fails, then WirekitError::Decode is returned and no panic occurs.
Given missing credentials, when a request is prepared, then WirekitError::InvalidConfig is returned and no request is sent.

userStories.title: Keep the crate safe, dependency-honest, and lint-clean
userStories.want: the crate to stay within its stated job
userStories.benefit: it can be a dependency of any Rust application

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the crate root, when compiled, then #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and #![deny(missing_docs)] are present and every public item is documented.
Given the crate, when built with default features and with each provider feature independently, then it compiles, and features are additive (CON-204).
Given Rust 1.85, when the workspace builds, then wirekit compiles under edition 2021.
Given the crate, when inspected, then it introduces no database, tenant, billing, or application-domain types (CON-106, CON-107).
Given the crate's source, when scanned, then it does not read .env files or environment files to obtain credentials (CON-519).
Given the full test suite, when it runs, then every acceptance criterion has at least one test, supplied by the Test agent (CON-404).

functionalRequirements.text: The repository MUST contain a wirekit crate as a workspace member at crates/wirekit, version 0.1.0, inheriting edition, rust-version, and license from [workspace.package].
The crate MUST compile with default = [], always expose the core, and gate every provider module behind an additive feature.
The crate MUST declare #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and #![deny(missing_docs)], and every public item MUST have a rustdoc comment.
A single #[non_exhaustive] WirekitError enum MUST be the only error type on the public API.
Every WirekitError variant MUST expose a stable code() string of the form W#### and MUST implement Display and std::error::Error.
Provider failures MUST map into WirekitError::Api { status, code, message }; a provider MUST NOT introduce a second error type.
WirekitError's Debug, Display, logs, traces, and payloads MUST NOT contain credentials, tokens, or raw bodies.
HTTP retries MUST use exponential backoff with jitter and 3 attempts by default.
Retries MUST occur on 5xx, 429, and network or timeout errors, and MUST honor Retry-After.
Retries MUST NOT occur on any other 4xx status.
The retry policy MUST be configurable per client for attempt count, base delay, maximum delay, and jitter bounds.
Rate limiting MUST be a per-provider token bucket with per-provider overrides.
The rate limiter MUST emit a tracing event for every rate-limit hit.
The crate MUST share one pooled reqwest::Client per process unless the caller injects its own client.
The client builder MUST allow configuring timeouts, TLS, proxying, and default headers.
The client MUST reject non-HTTPS base URLs with WirekitError::InvalidConfig.
The auth layer MUST provide Bearer, Basic, API-key-in-header, API-key-in-query, HMAC-signature, and OAuth2-client-credentials schemes.
OAuth2 client credentials MUST fetch a token, cache it, and refresh it before expiry, with a single in-flight fetch per client.
Auth and secret types MUST redact secrets in Debug/Display and MUST NOT implement Serialize for a secret field.
Every outbound request MUST emit tracing events for start, finish with duration, retry, rate-limit hit, and error.
The core MUST expose one request pipeline (auth, rate limit, retry, send, decode) so a provider supplies only a URL, method, body, and response type.
The core MUST expose a body-level error hook so that HTTP 200 with a body-reported error maps to WirekitError::Api.
Response bodies MUST decode into caller types via serde, and a decode failure MUST return WirekitError::Decode rather than a panic.
The crate MUST treat URLs, header values, and response bytes as untrusted and MUST NOT panic on malformed input.
Credentials MUST come from caller-supplied configuration or secret stores; the crate MUST NOT read .env or environment files.
The crate MUST be publishable as wirekit 0.1.0 with complete metadata and a docs.rs all-features configuration.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST compile on Rust 1.85 with edition 2021.
The crate MUST keep forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs); docs MUST build with warnings denied.
Features MUST be additive; enabling a provider feature MUST NOT enable or disable another feature, and the default feature set MUST be documented.
The crate MUST NOT force a database, tenant model, quota state, webhook state, or application-domain types on consumers.
Retry backoff and token-bucket waiting MUST yield to the async runtime and MUST NOT block a runtime thread.
The shared client MUST bound resource usage through default timeouts and connection-pool limits.
Secrets MUST be redacted in Debug, Display, logs, traces, and error payloads, and MUST NOT be serialized.
The crate MUST treat all network input as untrusted and MUST NOT panic, abort, or hang on malformed responses.
Every acceptance criterion MUST be covered by at least one test, supplied by the Test agent.
The crate MUST NOT expose a global mutable singleton; client and provider construction MUST be explicit.
Authentication (CON-511) - the pipeline MUST apply the configured auth scheme to every outbound request and MUST fail closed with WirekitError::InvalidConfig when credentials are missing.
Rate limiting (CON-514) - the per-provider token bucket MUST be enforced before every outbound request, with per-provider overrides.
Input validation (CON-515) - URLs, header values, and response bodies MUST be validated; malformed input MUST return a typed WirekitError and MUST NOT panic.
Environment security (CON-519) - credentials MUST come from caller-supplied configuration or secret stores; the crate MUST NOT read .env files and MUST NOT commit secrets.
HTTPS (CON-520) - all outbound requests MUST use TLS; non-HTTPS base URLs MUST be rejected before any socket is opened.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Wait at least the header value, then retry; if attempts are exhausted, return WirekitError::RateLimit { retry_after }.
Apply jittered exponential backoff.
WirekitError::Api carrying the last status and any parsed code and message.
No retry; WirekitError::Api returned immediately.
Retried, then WirekitError::Network.
Retried, then WirekitError::Timeout.

edgeCases.description: Retry-After given as an HTTP date, or unparseable
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Parsed safely; an unparseable value falls back to backoff without panicking.
The request waits asynchronously and proceeds when a token is available.
WirekitError::Auth; no retry on a non-429 4xx.
Refreshed before the next request, never during a partially sent one.

edgeCases.description: HTTP 200 with Slack ok: false or a GraphQL errors[] array
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: WirekitError::Api via the body-level error hook (CON-213).
WirekitError::Decode; no panic.
Rejected before any socket is opened.
Used verbatim; no second pool and no overridden configuration.
Share one bucket so the aggregate rate is respected.
Debug prints ***; Serialize is not implemented for the secret.
Bounded by a configurable limit; exceeding it returns a typed error rather than an unbounded allocation.
WirekitError::InvalidConfig; no request is sent.
Computed over the raw request bytes; a re-serialized body would not verify.
Refresh uses a configurable safety margin.

dependencies.name: reqwest
dependencies.notes: HTTP client with rustls-tls by default; the single shared client per process (CON-210).

dependencies.name: tokio
dependencies.notes: Async runtime features rt, time, and macros; required by the retry and rate-limit timers.

dependencies.name: tracing
dependencies.notes: Request, retry, rate-limit, and error events (CON-211).

dependencies.name: serde_json
dependencies.notes: JSON encoding and decoding for provider bodies.

dependencies.name: http
dependencies.notes: Shared HTTP types: HeaderMap, StatusCode, Method.

dependencies.name: async-trait
dependencies.notes: Object-safe async auth and transport traits.

dependencies.name: wiremock
dependencies.notes: Dev-dependency only: local HTTP mock for provider tests.

dependencies.name: crates.io
dependencies.notes: Publication target (BP-010); the wirekit name MUST be checked immediately before publish (CON-111).

dependencies.name: GitHub Actions
dependencies.notes: Workspace and MSRV CI from BP-002.

risks.description: A single crate carrying 26+ provider features becomes a release and build-time bottleneck.
risks.mitigation: Ship core only in this feature; measure build times and propose a companion crate if needed (CON-104 amendment path).

risks.description: 0.x churn in the error, retry, or auth contract breaks provider modules.
risks.mitigation: #[non_exhaustive], stable W#### codes, and an additive-only feature policy until the 1.0 freeze.

risks.description: A dependency raises its MSRV above 1.85.
risks.mitigation: The MSRV CI job fails fast; pin or downgrade with a recorded decision.

risks.description: rustls versus native-tls surprises on a platform.
risks.mitigation: rustls is the default and a documented feature selects native-tls.

risks.description: A secret leaks into logs, traces, or an error payload.
risks.mitigation: The Secret<T> wrapper, no Serialize for secret fields, redacted tracing fields, and property tests from the Test agent.

risks.description: A provider needs behavior the pipeline cannot express.
risks.mitigation: The body-level error hook, per-provider retry and rate-limit overrides, and injectable clients.

risks.description: The rate limiter blocks the async runtime or is unfair under concurrency.
risks.mitigation: Async token acquisition, per-provider buckets, and the concurrency edge case EC-015.

risks.description: Scope creeps into provider modules or stateful crates.
risks.mitigation: The explicit out-of-scope list; later work becomes new features (CON-604, CON-612).
